english.title: Attempt to cause a male aged 13 or over to engage in sexual activity - no penetration
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) attempted to cause a

(A)_[boy aged13]_
(B)_[boy aged14]_
(C)_[boy aged15]_
(D)_[man aged 16 or over]_

to engage in sexual activity of a non penetrative nature, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACTIVITY..), with intent to do so when he did not consent and you did not reasonably believe that he was consenting
english.legislation: Contrary to section 1(1) of the Criminal Attempts Act 1981.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
attempted to cause
a boy aged 13 / 14 / 15 / man aged 16 or over
to engage in a
sexual activity of a non penetrative nature
with intent to do so
you not reasonably believing that he had consented

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) See section 72 of, and Schedule 2 to, the Sexual Offences Act 2003 regarding the committing of this offence outside the UK by UK nationals / residents.
(ii) A person guilty of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 19).
(iii) Whether a belief is reasonable is to be determined having regard to all the circumstances, including any steps the offender has taken to ascertain whether the victim consented - (section 4(2)).
(iv) Victim's age should be proved by reference to a Birth Certificate where possible.

other.penalty:
Summary: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: Ten years imprisonment

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
